sample.rationale: Tract Mirror is literally LPC's central thesis built into a shipped VST — the strongest spawned relation in the room, and it answers LPC's own open question about whether the source-filter identity is only a prose claim. Currently only Tract Mirror points back (emerged-from); LPC has no forward pointer to what it produced.
sample.evidence: "The thesis is the mirrors link from [[Linear Predictive Coding]] to [[Waveguide Synthesizer]], executed: the LPC lattice filter's reflection coefficients are the impedance mismatches between successive tube segments." — Tract Mirror

sample.rationale: This entry names 'control-surface design for high-dimensional spaces' as the suite's single hardest, most valuable, unsolved problem. control-vocabulary-math is a shipped, worked instance of exactly that problem solved for a sibling instrument — a noisy N-neuron Kuramoto population reduced to four performable knobs (K, sigma_threshold, mean firing rate, and the order parameter r as both readout and control term).
sample.evidence: "A 256-dimensional latent space, a family of triply-periodic minimal surfaces, a persistence diagram — each is a rich object with no existing performance vocabulary... That invention — not the DSP — is where the value and the difficulty concentrate." — Infeasible DSP Now Shippable; "This document formalizes the layer that sits on top of that engine: the statistical descriptors that turn a noisy crowd of N spiking neurons into four or five smooth, performable knobs." — control-vocabulary-math

sample.rationale: LPC declares this mirrors link explicitly ('LPC's lattice and the digital waveguide are the same structure read from opposite ends'), and Tract Mirror carries the same claim from a third angle, but Waveguide Synthesizer's own frontmatter is silent on it — the triangle is missing its third leg.
sample.evidence: "That is why the link to [[Waveguide Synthesizer]] is a mirrors and not a passing reference: the vocal tract and the plucked string are one piece of mathematics wearing two bodies." — Linear Predictive Coding
